title: A Passage for the Provision
premise: Dominic Fairweather has spent a decade outrunning the shadow of his famous archaeologist father, Marcus, whose expeditions made headlines and whose absence made orphans of his children. When Marcus's river expedition into the remote Velloran basin goes silent mid-monsoon season, Dominic is the only one who knows the waterways well enough to mount a rescue. Aboard a leaking boat with Wren Calloway, his father's estranged research partner who carries her own grudge against Marcus, Dominic navigates flooded gorges, hostile salvagers, and the ruins his father sought — discovering that Marcus's final inheritance is not treasure but proof that he chose family over glory at the end. The rescue becomes a reckoning: Dominic must decide whether to bury his father's legacy with his resentment or claim it as his own.
about_author: Edmund Ashgrove is the pen name of a former river guide turned novelist who spent six seasons working the tributaries of Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. His debut draws on firsthand knowledge of monsoon country and the people who make their living on its unpredictable waters.

chapters.title: The Man Who Keeps Moving
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He finishes a salvage job in a port town and leaves before dawn, avoiding a letter forwarded from his father's foundation. Establishes his restless code: never stay long enough to owe anyone anything. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as freedom.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A telegram reaches him: Marcus's expedition upriver has missed three scheduled check-ins. The foundation wants to wait; Dominic calculates the monsoon window and realizes waiting means never finding them. He decides to go, telling himself it's about the boat fee they'll pay him. Beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Calloway, Marcus's former research partner, is trying to charter a boat herself when she recognizes Dominic at the docks. They haven't spoken since she testified against Marcus in an academic scandal years ago. She offers money and maps; he refuses her company. Beat: mutual distrust.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. No other pilot will take the run this late in the season. Wren finds him anyway, and they strike a cold bargain: she rides along, stays out of the wheelhouse, and pays double. First hints that her stake in the expedition is personal. Beat: uneasy alliance sealed in rain.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The journey begins through narrowing gorges. Dominic tests Wren with questions about his father; her answers are careful, evasive. A near-collision with a logjam forces them to work together for the first time. Beat: grudging respect taking root.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a trading post, Wren reveals fragments of the old scandal: Marcus was accused of forging provenance papers, and Wren's testimony ended both their careers. She insists she lied under pressure from the foundation. Dominic doesn't believe her. Beat: the past surfaces.

chapters.title: The Leaking Hull
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The boat develops a seam leak below the waterline. Repairs cost them a full day and most of their spare caulking. Dominic realizes someone at the dock may have loosened the planking — sabotage meant to stop any rescue. Beat: vulnerability exposed.

chapters.title: Salvagers at Sarn's Reach
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They're boarded by river salvagers led by a woman named Odile Voss, who claims Marcus hired her crew weeks ago and then cut them loose without pay. She wants compensation; she also knows where the expedition last anchored. Beat: new threat, new information.

chapters.title: The Last Anchorage
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Following Voss's directions, they find the expedition's base camp abandoned — tents stripped, equipment stacked neatly, a journal page weighted under a stone. The page says only: 'Moving inland. D. should understand why.' Beat: hope sharpened by dread.

chapters.title: Why Me
chapters.summary: Night camp, Wren's POV. Wren asks why Marcus would leave a message addressed to Dominic. Dominic admits he hasn't spoken to his father in nine years — since the night he refused to join the family business of digging up the dead. Beat: grief disguised as anger.

chapters.title: Inland Track
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They leave the boat moored with a paid watchman and follow the trail inland through rising floodwater. Signs of the party ahead: boot prints, a discarded instrument case, fresh-cut vines. Someone is moving fast and light. Beat: pursuit energy.

chapters.title: The Bridge Out
chapters.summary: Shared POV. A swollen river has taken the rope bridge. Crossing means swimming the flood channel; Wren nearly drowns and Dominic pulls her out. In the aftermath she tells him the real reason she came: Marcus sent her a private letter a month ago asking forgiveness. Beat: first crack in Dominic's armor.

chapters.title: Voss Follows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They spot Voss's crew on their backtrail, better armed and better supplied. Wren argues they should confront or evade; Dominic chooses a decoy route through karst caves. Inside, ancient carvings hint at what Marcus was really hunting. Beat: tension ratchets.

chapters.title: The Map Beneath the Map
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Studying the carvings, Wren recognizes Marcus's notation system on a rubbing left behind — he'd found a site the foundation never knew about, one he kept off every official record. Dominic understands: his father went dark on purpose. Beat: the mission reframes.

chapters.title: Monsoon Breaks
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The full monsoon hits. They shelter in a cave with two of Marcus's porters, half-drowned and separated from the main group. The porters reveal the expedition split: some followed the patron's man inland, others fled. There is a patron — and he wanted the site for himself. Beat: stakes widen.

chapters.title: The Patron's Man
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The porters name Aldous Renner, a collector's agent who funded the expedition covertly and now holds leverage over several crew members. Wren realizes the forged-provenance scandal years ago traces back to Renner too — Marcus was framed to keep him compliant. Beat: old wounds recontextualized.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Renner's men catch them at a river ford. In the fight, one porter is taken and the journal page stolen. Dominic gets his first look at Renner himself across the water — urbane, unhurried, certain. Beat: the enemy gains a face.

chapters.title: Blood in the Water
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Aftermath of the ambush. The injured porter needs care; they detour to a riverside village where a healer owes Wren an old debt. Villagers speak of 'the quiet foreigner' who passed through paying debts and mending roofs — Marcus, behaving like a different man. Beat: Dominic's image of his father wavers.

chapters.title: A Different Man
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The village headman shows Dominic a photograph Marcus left as thanks: Marcus holding a local child, laughing. Dominic can't reconcile it with the father who missed everything. Wren watches him struggle and says nothing, letting the picture do its work. Beat: quiet devastation.

chapters.title: The Watchman's Tale
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Returning briefly to check the boat, they find the watchman gone and the vessel stripped of fuel — Voss's crew. But Voss left a note: she'll trade fuel for a share of whatever Marcus found. She's been tracking Renner too, for her unpaid wages. Beat: enemies become reluctant allies.

chapters.title: Three-Way Bargain
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Negotiation scene around a driftwood fire. Voss supplies fuel and muscle; Dominic pilots; Wren negotiates terms sharp enough that even Voss smiles. Alliances are provisional, everyone armed, no one trusting anyone. Beat: momentum restored, danger doubled.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Bells
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The route narrows into a gorge where hanging stones chime in the wind — the landmark from Marcus's rubbing. Navigating it at flood stage nearly kills them all, and Dominic's piloting saves the boat. Voss, watching, revises her opinion of him aloud. Beat: earned competence, earned regard.

chapters.title: First Ruins
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach the outer ruins: terraces drowned to their shoulders, a causeway surfacing at low water. Wren reads the iconography and realizes the site records a civilization that survived its own great flood — a people who built for water instead of against it. Beat: wonder amid peril.

chapters.title: Signs of Life
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Fresh smoke. They find a lean-to with recent ashes and a tin cup Dominic recognizes from childhood — his father's, dented the same way. Someone is alive and close. Hope arrives so hard it hurts. Beat: emotional spike.

chapters.title: Renner's Camp
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Before they can reach the smoke, they stumble on Renner's forward camp: crates, radios, and two of Marcus's crew held 'for their protection.' Voss creates a diversion; Dominic and Wren free the captives, learning Marcus traded himself to Renner for the others' release. Beat: sacrifice revealed.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The freed crew explain the bargain: Marcus agreed to hand over the site's location if Renner let his people evacuate before the worst flooding. Renner agreed because he needs Marcus alive to open the inner vault. Wren sees the shape of a plan forming. Beat: strategy over despair.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They intercept the evacuation party heading downriver and reunite survivors with the porters. Among them, Marcus's young assistant Ilsa gives Dominic a message his father dictated weeks ago: 'Tell my son the provision was never the gold.' Dominic doesn't yet know what it means. Beat: mystery deepens, heart opens.

chapters.title: What Was Never Gold
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren deciphers the phrase using the site's own inscriptions: the 'provision' is the flood archive — seed stores, water engineering, a record of survival meant to be inherited by whoever came after. Marcus wasn't hunting treasure; he was protecting a legacy for his children. Beat: thematic revelation.

chapters.title: Renner Closes
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Renner's main force moves on the inner vault with Marcus as reluctant guide. Voss proposes hitting their supply line instead of a frontal assault; Dominic argues for speed. The group splits roles for the climax approach. Beat: gathering storm.

chapters.title: The Vault Road
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Night ascent through flooded terraces toward the vault entrance. Dominic recalls being taught to read strata as a boy — his father's hands over his — and realizes those memories were the inheritance all along. Beat: reconciliation with the past begun.

chapters.title: Father and Son
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They reach the vault chamber as Renner forces Marcus to breach the seal. Father and son see each other across the torchlight — nine years of silence in one look. Marcus's voice breaks on Dominic's name. Beat: the reunion, raw and unfinished.

chapters.title: The Water Rises
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The seal breached, meltwater and monsoon flood begin pouring into the lower chambers exactly as the archive's builders designed — a defense. Renner refuses to retreat, ordering crates loaded while the water climbs. Beat: countdown established.

chapters.title: Standoff in the Rising Dark
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Climax begins. Wren confronts Renner with evidence of the old forgery — she kept the originals all these years, protection she never used until now. Renner's men falter as the water takes the lower gallery. Beat: truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Voss's Price
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Voss turns on Renner, choosing wages over loyalty, and pins his guards while the water surges. Renner, cornered, tries to take the archive index and swim for it. Marcus goes after him into the flood. Beat: sacrifice looms again.

chapters.title: The Handhold
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Climax peak. Dominic reaches his father in the torrent and holds him against the current — the son pulling the father out, reversing every old current between them. Renner loses the index and his freedom to the water. Beat: love against duty resolved in action.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Dawn above the gorge. Survivors count themselves; the archive's upper chambers survive, accessible and documented properly this time. Marcus, exhausted, begins to apologize and Dominic stops him — there will be time, if they both choose to stay. Beat: exhale.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Downriver, Wren delivers her preserved documents to the authorities, clearing Marcus's name and ending Renner's operation. Voss is paid in full plus salvage rights honestly negotiated. Debts settled, she salutes Dominic and departs. Beat: justice and release.

chapters.title: The Provision
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV (first time). Marcus explains his silence: shame kept him away, and the expedition was his attempt to leave something worthy instead of excuses. He asks nothing — only whether Dominic might want to document the site together, as partners. Beat: invitation without demand.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic repairs the old boat rather than selling it — the first thing he's ever chosen to keep. He and Wren chart the site's preservation plan, arguing comfortably about methods. He mails a reply to the foundation under his own name. Beat: stillness chosen, not feared.

chapters.title: A Passage Kept
chapters.summary: Shared closing POV. Months later, the site opens to proper study with Dominic as field director, Wren as archivist, Marcus as consultant who knows when to be quiet. On the gorge wind, the bells ring, and Dominic finally stops moving — because staying, he learns, costs only what you're willing to give. Beat: homecoming.
